response.goal: Fix our n8n workflow so the full CSV file of about 5,000 rows lands in Google Sheets every night without failing due to rate limits, including retries and a Slack message if it still fails.

plan.step: Analyze the existing n8n workflow and diagnose the Google Sheets 429 Too Many Requests error on large batch inserts.
Redesign the data import logic to process rows in smaller chunks with built-in batching, delays, or pagination to respect Google Sheets API rate limits.
Implement robust error handling, automated retry logic, and a Slack alert notification if the import fails after retries.
Test the updated workflow with a full-size dataset and verify nightly execution stability.

milestones.name: Diagnosis and Redesign
milestones.deliverable: Updated n8n workflow structure featuring batching logic to bypass Google Sheets rate limits.

milestones.name: Error Handling and Final Testing
milestones.deliverable: Fully tested workflow containing automated retries and Slack failure alerts.

risks.risk: Google Sheets API quotas might continue to restrict write operations even with modified batch sizes.
risks.mitigation: Implement appropriate wait nodes or batch chunking to stay well within Google API rate limits.

risks.risk: The fixed budget of $250 assumes the existing n8n structure is straightforward to refactor.
risks.mitigation: Review the workflow structure immediately upon project start to confirm scope aligns with the budget.

questions: Are you using self-hosted n8n or n8n cloud, and do you have access to execution logs?

assumptions: The client will provide access to the existing n8n instance and Google Sheets/Slack credentials for testing.
